en: Those who join us that way,
I will call "subordinate Nosferatu"
from now on.
You can give direct Nosferatu a dispatch,
which lets you command them directly.
Subordinates act the same as direct ones do.
note: JP: subordinates behave as their direct Nosferatu does; kept general

en: The other difference is that
direct ones can build up their numbers,
but subordinates can't.
If possible, I'd like to see capable people
made into direct Nosferatu.
Critical Vitality...
I'm about to tell you something important,
so listen carefully.
To beat the enemy Vampir and win this war,
you have to increase this Critical Vitality,
and there's no other way...
To increase Critical Vitality,
you have to share your own Critical Vitality
note: object/verb order swapped in English: 2578 holds the verb "share", 2579 "with your Nosferatu"

en: with your Nosferatu.
If a Nosferatu is female,
she'll take the Critical Vitality you gave her,
note: "she" - sentence sets up female Nosferatu in #2580

en: and double it overnight for you.
A male Nosferatu, on the other hand,
will mostly fight enemy Dhampir,
to take their Critical Vitality.
Conversely, if a Nosferatu loses a battle,
the Critical Vitality you shared gets taken away.
Each Nosferatu has a limit on how much
Critical Vitality they can hold. Past it,
they can't retain any more.
A Nosferatu with no Critical Vitality that night
can't hear your commands,
and can't do anything. Be careful.
Even if a Nosferatu loses a battle,
they won't die,
and they won't turn back into humans either.
As for the fighting at night, your familiar
Sistina will report to you as it happens,
so listen carefully.
Before dawn, you'll see how your Nosferatu
fought and how Critical Vitality changed.
Ideally, you'll learn to judge the situation and give
your direct Nosferatu the right instructions.
Those who call themselves "vampire hunters"
are humans you must be very careful of.
They gather rumors from the residents by day,
and attack us directly at night.
If a door has "garlic," "holly," or an "altar"
on it, someone is trying to seal vampires out.
That's the hunters' handiwork.
You can remove them during the day,
but touching one unawares at night means
note: toucher left unspecified (JP elides it); gerund keeps it neutral

en: taking damage, so be careful.
The "altar" is especially dangerous. Any
Nosferatu who touches it is "purified,"
and turns back into a human.
If the vampire hunters discover our
residence, we're in a bit of trouble.
They're after the coffins we rest in...
If they find it and break open our coffins,
your stats, like "Vitality" and "Blood Flow,"
can no longer be recovered...
If your residence gets found out,
note: Also listed under msgs 66581/70938/103189/107285 (Ios, Southwark, Wendy, Johanna) where the text shows only this fragment: looks like a stray reference; not varianted. Self-contained for 135364 (no residence mentioned on its first page)

en: use "Wait" there to repair the coffins.
That's best.
I wish I had enough power to stand
against them...
, I can't be of more help to you.
note: follows {PLAYER_NAME}; with #2629 "I'm sorry." (shared with msgs 143435/143469, where it follows "...I want to be more useful")

en: I'm sorry.
note: shared: 135291, 143435, 143469; reads as a plain apology in all three

en: If the hunters break open our coffins,
Some vampire hunters are said to have
note: reflowed across 2631-2633 (verb phrase moved); no content dropped

en: the power to purify Nosferatu and turn
them back into humans.
Those hunters are hateful, but
you could also turn the tables and use them.
Among the residents and the hunters,
you spread false rumors.
With luck, you can steer the hunters toward the enemy's
stronghold.
